thread.title: Dougie’s Friday mailbag (Ryan Garcia, Lennox Lewis vs. Showtime, the WBO, Marciano)

author: Doug Fischer
title: Dougie’s Friday mailbag (Ryan Garcia, Lennox Lewis vs. Showtime, the WBO, Marciano)
text:
The modern day gatekeeper mythical matchup: 
Darnell Boone v Dashon Johnson @ 160? 
Thanks. – Ste, Manchester 
Damn, that’s a good one. Well done, Ste. Darnell Boone, AKA The Godfather of Gatekeepers! 
This is a difficult matchup to figure, but I’m going to go with the O.G., the Godfather of Gatekeepers, which is Boone. Johnson is the better athlete of the two, but I think Boone is naturally bigger, the harder puncher and craftier. (Plus, he’s from Youngstown, Ohio, so I gotta give him a slight edge just for that.) 
I think Deezol wins a close decision in an entertaining fight. 
You know who would be a good person to pose this mythical matchup to? Gennady Golovkin, who has used both in sparring for obvious reasons. In fact, Johnson will be part of GGG’s sparring for the Canelo rematch, along with another decorated middleweight/super middleweight gatekeepr, Derrick Findley. 
Come to think of it, if Boone and Johnson ever fought for real, Findley would have to get a crack at the winner for the G.O.G title. 

THE ULTIMATE BOXER 
Hey Dougie,I don’t know if anyone has already asked you this, but rather than a mythical matchup, how about a mythical fighter? If you could build your ideal fighter by combining the punches (jab/straight/cross/hook/uppercut), defence, chin and conditioning of any fighters, what would you choose? And who would be in his corner? Keep up the awesome work dude! – Jamie, UK 
Thanks, Jamie. Will do. 
How about Joe Louis’ jab, Thomas Hearns’ straight (right), Rocky Marciano’s (right) cross, Sugar Ray Robinson’s (left) hook, Mike Tyson’s uppercut, Pernell Whitaker’s defense, Marvin Hagler’s chin and Henry Armstrong’s conditioning/stamina, and Emanuel Steward training him (with in-the-gym assistance from Bill Miller and Luther Burgess)? 
Does that sound like a formidable fighter to you? 

THANKS! 
Another great Mail Bag!! Keep them coming Doug!! That’s it. – Marvin 
I’ll take it, Marvin. Thank you! And I will keep them coming. (As my buddy Steve Kim likes to say, this beats having a real job.) 

Email Fischer at [email protected] . Follow him on Twitter at @dougiefischer Share this story Left Hook2 
Perfect fighter…..’and RJJ’s speed and reflexes, Floyd’s business savvy, and Artuto Gatti’s heart’ 
Orgs being recognized–they only become recognized when it becomes advantageous to the fighter/promoter/network. If Showtime can say they have a championship fight, they aren’t really concerned what initials are attached. That is why I prefer to ignore the belts, and only rank the fighters. To prove they are the best…they must beat the best…don’t defend against bottom tier fighters. That is like Ohio State beating the Citadel in football 70–0 each week. Yeah, looks good. Proves nothing about how elite they are until they face Bama. Stephen M 
And Tyson Fury’s mouth… Robert Archambault 
…should be permanently sealed with crazy glue. Giuseppe 
Boone knocked down Ward, Kovalev and Stevenson, didn’t he? legendary. Jorge 
De La Hoya was fighting grown ass men in his 17th fight (John John Molina). After that he fought Rafael Ruelas and Genaro Hernandez. Those standards are very high almost for any fighter. Let Garcia develop. Left Hook2 
How great he was truly does get overlooked sometimes. Those guys were not paper champs…they were true champs that he fought. philoe bedoe 
He was also the box office draw in his fights. A lot of boxers in that position wouldn’t have been matched that tough during their careers………….. Tony Nightstick 
While Doug’s assessment of Marciano is fair and reasonable, I’d rank him higher. I definitely have him among my Top 5 heavyweights. Also, while I agree that he’s probably not a pound-for-pound ATG, I think he should be among the Top 10 greatest Italian-American fighters. 
As for the mythical perfect fighter — a good question and a tough one to answer. I think Doug’s composite is pretty good, though I’d probably have Ray Arcel in his corner. Jayo2.0 
I can think of a few dozen heavyweights that would be Marciano. Top 5? Not a chance. wrecksracer 
You would think that the size of modern heavyweights alone would create a lot of problems for Marciano. On the other hand, modern heavyweights tend to gas mid fight. Marciano could literally lose 14 and 1/2 rounds and still win by knockout by the end of the fight. He was an uncommonly powerful puncher with an unreal gas tank. I’m not so sure he would be beaten easily by any heavyweight. Especially guys who would have problems going 15 hard rounds. Stephen M 
Big guys who know how to use their size and weight to wear down smaller guys would beat him. He Marciano would be tiny in there against guys like Lennox Lewis, the Klitschkos, Tyson Fury etc.. Those big guys all used their height and weight to rough up and wear out smaller guys like Povetkin, Tyson and Cunningham… wrecksracer 
In Marciano’s case, he won by guys getting tired from hitting him. Lol….well, they would probably win on cuts. I’m not sure it was possible to knock him out. william ellis 
Good mailbag Doug – the problem with ranking Marciano goes even farther: he was a modern Cruiserweight. His top weight was 189 lbs. But come to think of it, almost all the Heavyweight champions before Liston were Cruiserweights – only Jeffries, Johnson, Willard, and Carnera fought consistently above 200 lbs. It was only with Liston that Heavyweights began consistently to weigh more than 200 lbs. 
I think Marciano is a pound-for-pound all-time-great, as were a lot of the earlier heavyweight champs who fought under 200 lbs, but if they weighed now what they weighed then they wouldn’t belong in the same ring with current Heavyweights. They would be massacred – like Bob Foster, a great fighter in his own weight class, was by Ali. 
Of course, people are bigger now in general, so maybe if Marciano were a young fighter now he would be bigger than he actually was – maybe the size of Frasier or Tyson. Ditto for Dempsey, Tunney, Louis, Charles, and so on. In that case the earlier champions would hold their own – but really only in that case. mikescapes 
I’d go further. Cruisers are up to 200lbs. these days. I don’t believe Marciano would be a top cruiser today. Listed at 5’11” ( I doubt it), short reach, he’d be in with much bigger, longer guys. I know you have to judge an athlete according to his performance during the era he was active. But we’re speculating here. Same day weigh-in he’s mid 180s tops without worrying about weight at heavyweight. Now, 2 day weigh-in, a monster like Gassiev is what? 210-215. So Rocky is out of luck. 
Should be: 190lbs. Cruiser limit; 215 lbs. Heavyweight limit; 215 and above Superheavyweight. Same day weigh-in. I’ll keep dreaming on. wrecksracer 
What if the modern cruisers had to fight under the rules at Marciano’s time? Same Day weigh in. 15 round fight. mikescapes 
Then they would have to abide by those rules. I forgot about the 15 rounders. Not sure I agree or disagree with 12 rounds. But if you fast forward Rocky into the future, he wouldn’t be around for 15 against these big cats. If you transport the modern Cruisers back in time I think they might be big slow and overweight, beatable, by Rocky. Weight is always a concern. That’s why weight classes are so important. It’s the equalizer. Stephen M 
I think that the light heavies probably weigh near to what Marciano weighed in the ring. Dee Money 
I’ll add this, the early 50’s were not the best era for heavyweights to begin with, not writing it was as bad as the mid 00’s but definitely far from the top. 
Moreover, I think Marciano gets a big bump from having the “0” in his record; but look more closely at the competition. In the same calendar year he beat a post retirement Joe Louis he fought three fighters who actually had losing records. Say what you will about the opponents of Wilder and Joshua they are no Harold Mitchell. 
On a P4P measure, looking at him as a relative Cruiserweight, Marciano is maybe a top 50 all time guy at best, but nowhere near a top 25 and I can think of several prime heavies who are clearly better than he in the ring. DRE 
Probably the biggest knock against Marciano was that his biggest wins were against old men. Okay then but Jersey Joe Walcot was coming off his career best win over Ezzard Charles before fighting The Rock. And Charles himself was knocking out heavyweight contenders which earned him the right to challenge Rocky. Even Joe Louis, as faded as he was still scored a few good KO wins prior to his run in with Marciano. So while those men were still past their primes they were still dangerous opponents. And all the credit to Marciano for finishing off in such brutal fashion. Even at 190 the man was a total wrecking-ball. As good as today’s cruisers are I think The Rock would have flattened each one of them. Not easily but if he were around today he’ll win the Muhammad Ali trophy for sure. As for the “bigger being better” theory, yes that often holds true but two of the most devastating punchers in heavyweight history, mainly Jack Dempsey and Joe Louis were indeed cruiserweights but were notorious for demolishing men much bigger than they were. If anything it was smaller faster guys that both Dempsey and Louis had more trouble with. Prime examples: Louis nearly losing to 168 pound Billie Conn and Dempsey being unable to get much done against some fat little guy named Willie Neeham (If that was the name. Correct me if I’m wrong) Would have Dempsey and Louis stomped over today’s giants. Hard to say. But they just might have. Another thing. Back in those days if you were 32 or more you were old. If you’re that age now you’re in your prime. John Newman 
Mr Fischer, clenbuterol is inexpensive, easy to obtain, and obviously not a designer PED. However, it’s also highly effective and comes with the ready made excuse of being meat-sourced for Mexican athletes. 
Canelo using clenbuterol is not at all close to Lance Armstrong buying from GNC. It’s a lot like Alberto Contador using it during his reign as the best sprinter in cycling, he couldn’t find a better PED (and he likely had access to more than Canelo and his unsophisticated team). In fact, their excuses for testing positive even resembled one another. 
But professional cycling had (and has) better investigations than the NAC. Stephen M 
Just one comment on this today from me. Victor Conte says in this interview that Clen would be ”very potent- for a boxer to use – very beneficial drug”. He also says that he believes that a lot of Mexicans use it. And that Canelo should do the hair test. Props to Cynthia by the way… https://www.youtube.com/watch?time_continue=72&v=nwcu7zYZO-Q Randall Bannister 
I think the hair test is the only real way to clear his name. If he hasn’t been cheating prior to this failed test, hair testing will show it. That’s why I don’t believe Canelo or the unsophisticated team he has around him. He has an easy way to prove his innocence yet he’s saying or doing nothing. 
He basically heading down to The Winchester, having a nice cold pint and waiting for this whole thing to blow over. AngelMorningstar 
This is how you KNOW that Doug does indeed DO WHAT ODLH tells him. In a mailbag he uses Conte as a excuse for Canelo in that the fans should ask him if Canelo would use that cheap crap. Conte says it would be great for a boxer and…. not a peep from Fisher. Stephen M 
Well, I don’t think that Oscar tells Doug what to do. But I do think that Doug is tip toeing around this thing. For example, he had no problems calling me “stupid” but if Canelo did eat tainted beef it’s because he is young and simple and unaware. It would seem to me that that would be a good time to bring out the word “stupid”. nick hapta 
just a heads up. Contador was a climbing and time trial specialist, sprinters dont win the tour & giro. He was suspended for 2 years with a much smaller amount of clen in his system than Alvarez. John Newman 
Thanks, I’ll make that change. I think I took the sprinting thing from an old Times article. I appreciate it. Jayo2.0 
Why is it that American writers (see Doug above) often claim that white and white-looking athletes who have feminine/gayish faces are “attractive”? I’m sorry, but Ryan Garcia is not one drop more “attractive” than Mike Tyson, Deontay Wilder, James Toney, etc., if anything, he is way less “attractive”. Robert Archambault 
You really are homophobic, aren’t you? Hiding something in your own closet perhaps? Methinks you protest a little too much. Jayo2.0 
All humans who don’t possess sodomite tendencies are ‘homophobic’. The reason you approve of it is because you know you would suck one under the right circumstances, and probably have. Fudge-packers and their defenders have bizarre logic. Randall Bannister 
So what kind of bloke is your type? If you don’t like the “feminine/gayish” look? Robert Archambault 
He seems to like the ones who can dominate and submit him. I bet he loves to watch MMA fighters with a great ground game. When a cop tells him to assume the position, he drops to all fours and presents his ass. LOL 🙂 Left Hook2 
If you watched the fight or have been to his fights, you will see plenty of females in the crowd. They are cheering for the “cute guy”, and could care less whether he was a boxer, baseball player, or construction worker. The point was that non-boxing fans were obviously enamored by Garcia in a Justin Bieber kind of way. wrecksracer 
Did you include James Toney and “attractive” in the same sentence? Charlie U. 
Why are you judging other guys’ looks? Robert Archambault 
I believe that no one told you to defend Canelo, Dougie, I really do, but that does not explain your complete flip in regards to the contaminated beef excuse from your previous statement that it was no longer a valid excuse. I would also like your opinion on the spin press release by GBP in regards to this when they totally avoided the FACT that there were TWO failed tests, not one, and that the first failed test showed much more than simple trace amounts that could be explained by contamination. Finally, the source of the substance makes no difference when it comes to sanctions. The basic FACT is that he failed TWO separate tests and must be made to pay a price for it. I will not speculate on what that penalty should be but he cannot be allowed to walk completely free from this situation as if nothing at all happened. If that is the case, I will no longer have any faith at all in any testing as a detriment to PED usage in the sport and they may as well let fighters use whatever the hell they want. Drop testing and bring back same day weigh ins and 15 round title fights and let the bodies fall where they may. Left Hook2 
What, in your opinion, should the penalty be that only impacts Canelo or the ‘dirty’ fighter? The sales pitch of combat sports is the individual in the ring, not a team, grouping, or tourney outcome. That makes it difficult to call off a fight—it hurts the opponent as well or even more. Do you think Canelo would still fight if 75% of his purse went to GGG and he had to wear 10 oz gloves? Or would he do like Margarito and take his show on the road? Robert Archambault 
At a minimum? 25% of his purse should go to CBP to pay for testing for fighters who do not make enough to pay for their own testing and to promote drug free boxing. IF Canelo refuses and decides to call off the fight, or if NSAC decide to halt the fight and suspend him, Canelo, his team and promoter should be held responsible to pay the entire purse of his opponent and a minimum 1 year suspension. If another GBP fighter tests positive within a 12 month period, GBP has their promoter license suspended for a year as well. Good enough? Tough enough to push fighters and promoters to do everything possible to clean up this shitty sport? Left Hook2 
I like it. The most important thing to me is that the clean fighter still gets paid. Robert Archambault 
Same here. The clean fighter should NEVER be forced to lose out due to an opponent failing a test. Wade Wilson 
Whatever happens the fighter who failed the test should not be allowed back until the benefits from the drug used have long since passed. A lot of users haven’t been able to get back to form when that happens. Tudor Pascanu 
In fact using whatever they want might just level the field in many fights-like in bodybuilding-they all ingest the crap so whoever works harder and has grater genetics wins DRE 
So once again Robert The Accuser hath spoken. The verdict: GUILTY!!! Let the witch hunt begin. Don Badowski 
Well, I thought I did a fair job of answering Dougie’s “why Clen” question on Monday. But I’ll add one more point. Anyone going with custom PEDs would be acting as their own guinea pig. Say what you will about clenbuterol, it is a know product with know benefits and side effects. Hey, even I wouldn’t go so far as to suggest that DLH set up a laboratory with a ward full of volunteers to test custom PEDs before they got fed to Alvarez. Or would I? No, I wouldn’t. None of this is going to matter to the NSAC. In the end they will put out a statement admonishing Team Canelo for not taking care before this oh so important event, and do nothing. No cancellation, no fine, no insistence that Alvarez submit to year round testing so that this doesn’t happen again. The NSAC will not release any details of its investigation. DLH will crow that the NSACs non-ruling is proof. Writers will put out articles about how nothing changes and money talks and business as usual. And we’ll buy the fight. Robert Archambault 
I’m surprised that no one has yet mentioned how much easier it would be for a fighter to use chemical ‘training aids’ when they know in advance exactly what two dates they will be fighting on each and every year. Is there any other fighter in the sport who knows exactly when they will be fighting, year in, year out, other than Canelo and previously Floyd? No, there is not. In fact, I would go as far as to state that in NO OTHER SPORT is there an athlete or team that knows the exact date each year of their next match or game or competition. Dates always change. Except for someone who only fights on the same two Mexican holidays each and every year. Having that fixed schedule makes it very easy to put a ‘training program’ in place that is basically undetectable when you are not subject to year round, random, testing. Something to think about, no? Don Badowski 
I’m sure lots of people have thought about it. And the answer to come back with is No. I suppose you saw my posts about how Golovkin is enrolled in VADA CBP and Alvarez is not. The WBC is supposed to be on board, a sponsor of VADA CBP. But they are also bending over backwards to get Alvarez back in the fold. So they put out half-truth statements about how Alvarez has been tested for 5 years. The WBC fails to mention the times when Alvarez decided to skip testing by VADA like for the Liam Smith fight. So you see, even when they profess to be taking a stand, they still look to business first. JV316 
just playing devil’s advocate here i’m kinda 50/50 on whether he cheated or not, but just a question, if it’s so easy when you know which two dates you’re fighting and when you’ll begin the testing regimen, then how in the hell did they just screw up and get caught? you’re ready to assume they’re stupid enough to get caught with a banned substance that supposedly only stays in the system for a few days when they know exactly when they’re fighting and when they’ll be tested, but you refuse to believe he’s stupid enough to eat tainted beef. seems like flawed logic to me. Robert Archambault 
First of all… I am presenting a hypothetical scenario and not making any claims. I’m just pointing out how much easier it would be for someone to abuse the rules when they have a fixed schedule for their fights that no other boxer or athlete in ANY OTHER SPORT has. I also did not say that he knows or knew exactly when he would be tested. In fact I believe that he was caught unawares by this test and did not expect to be tested before he moved his training camp to the US. . Second… I don’t care if he was deliberately cheating or not. He tested positive and he has a responsibility to monitor everything that enters his body. At the very least, he needs to be severely fined and if his claims of tainted beef cannot be proved, then he needs to be suspended. Ignorance is not an excuse. It does not work in a court of law and it should not be permitted to work here either. Maybe when testing Mexican fighters, their entire entourage should also be tested. This way if the fighter tests positive for clenbuterol, others in his team who eat with him and consume the same meals should also test positive. If they don’t, then there’s a problem somewhere. And in training camp, perhaps there needs to be a complete accounting of all food receipts so that any future event such at this can be properly investigated and the source of the meat traced and tested. JV316 
well he knew when the possibility of testing would begin. but you may be right, maybe vada has never tested him before he does his usual camp move to san diego and they relied on that history and were caught unexpectedly, although that seems like a pretty big gamble on their part. don’t disagree with your suggestions for a fine or accounting for what happens in training camp. 
by the way, ignorance is often an excuse that works in the court of law. it depends on the crime. there are plenty of judges and legal scholars who frown on strict liability. DRE 
So let me guess. You’re going to keep moaning about it on and on. Buy the fight, watch it and then let moaning continue. Good plan. Stephen M 
Ok, I’m a fool, so I’ll comment on William’s post… I don’t think that Oscar, or anyone at GBP, tells Dougie what to do. I also think that Doug is someone of integrity, intelligence and objectivity. Those things notwithstanding, it would be nice to see a disclosure somewhere, similar to what I see in articles about stocks. As an example, something along these lines: “Disclosure: I am/we are long BRK.A, BRK.B, AAPL, UNP, WFC, VOO. I wrote this article myself, and it expresses my own opinions. I am not receiving compensation for it (other than from Seeking Alpha). I have no business relationship with any company whose stock is mentioned in this article.”. These disclosures are warranted because everyone understands that someone with an interest is different from someone who has no interest in what they are reporting. 
The Ring is owned by GBP and Doug does commentating gigs for GBP. This does not disqualify Doug from doing his job but it is significant, and it is something that most readers would be interested in knowing. Robert Archambault 
I just want him to pick a position and stick with it. NO MATTER WHAT FIGHTER IS INVOLVED. Not too much to ask. Left Hook2 
Come on man…I consider Doug to be one of the ‘good guys’…use your vitriol on some of the other shills who have poor writing skills and obvious agendas. And changing positions is not illegal or even wrong. Sometimes new evidence tells a different story. Or different attitudes/focuses. Doug and the email entertains me…what more can I ask of it? Robert Archambault 
Look… a few weeks ago he made a post where he said it was time to stop accepting the Mexican beef excuse as a valid reason for failing a test. Then Canelo fails and uses the excuse and he is fine with it. Sorry, but I can’t give him a pass for that. And when he is called out for it, he starts insulting people left and right. He is too upstanding a guy for that kind of behavior. I’ve always respected his expertise regarding the sport and find it disappointing when he will not stand by his own word when it really matters. Charlie U. 
Stick to a position? You mean like someone swearing up and down that he would never post on a particular website again and then coming back to said website a few months later as if nothing happened?? philoe bedoe 
Great mailbag again Doug. As we’re talking about the heavyweight’s, how become there’s no talk anymore of all the best American heavyweight’s are either in basketball or football? Is that because there is a top heavyweight now called Deontay Wilder 
Top 6 Pound for Pound 1
